The Eternal Eaters.name: 永恒噬者 The Eternal Eaters
The Eternal Eaters.text:
永恒噬者

有人说人如其食，而永恒噬者则以最极端的字面意义来奉行此言。教派成员来自黄金之路（Golden Road）各处，他们坚信自己所吞噬的一切都将成为其灵魂不可分割的一部分，并随着他们前往来世的最终归宿。进食不仅是为了维持凡人身躯，更是为了充盈来世的宴席。牙齿为填满宝库而啃咬着人人渴求的传家宝与珍贵的宝石，咽喉为建造私人宫殿而粗粝地吞咽石材与金属。在最极端的情况下，成员甚至会吞噬心爱的宠物与家庭成员，以确保彼此能在永恒中团聚。每咬下一口都是对厄加图娅的奉献，以期盼她能够接纳这份虔诚，在她的神域之中赐予他们家园。

永恒噬者的身体会因为竭力消化这些异常饮食而承受巨大的痛苦。然而，他们将此种痛苦视为换取死后永恒快乐的微小代价，并拒绝任何缓解症状的医疗措施。当一名永恒噬者死亡后，他最后的奉献之举就是将自己的躯体献给厄加图娅，让它在凡间继续侍奉女神，而灵魂则会前往自己精心构筑的来世。

The Shepherds of Affliction.name: 苦难牧者 The Shepherds of Affliction
The Shepherds of Affliction.text:
苦难牧者

惊骇之眼（Eye of Dread）的居民曾经亲身领略，凡人在神明般的威胁面前是何等无力。当一些人蜷缩在英雄的盾牌后方，或将自己隔绝于废墟之中时，苦难牧者却相信，文明的存续之道在于培育强者和淘汰弱者。他们将厄加图娅奉为生存的巅峰，利用疾病作为其终极考验，以甄别谁有资格以她的名义继承这个世界。

苦难牧者来到一座座城镇，用毁灭性的疾病感染整个村庄并剥夺他们的药物。幸存者被纳入教派，获得充足的食物、军事训练以及用于对抗任何威胁的死灵术奥秘。那些不够格而死亡的人则会被唤起为不死仆从，被当作工具使唤，而非获得安息的尊严。极少数获得厄加图娅启示的人被尊为预言家，享有巨大的特权，但也被迫处于永远发烧的状态。每一天，苦难牧者的成员和力量都在增长，怀着不可动摇的信念前进，坚信他们试图建立的疾病肆虐的世界值得所有的牺牲。

The Ashen Church.name: 灰烬教会 The Ashen Church
The Ashen Church.text:
The Ashen Church

Cults dedicated to proliferating and venerating the undead are plentiful among Urgathoa's worshippers, but none are as successful as the Ashen Church. Appearing across Golarion where war, natural disaster, or extreme poverty have struck, the Ashen Church bears witness to the ways people become fearful, cruel, and desperate when faced with their own mortality. Members seek to alleviate this cycle of suffering by sharing the comfort their goddess offers: that one doesn't have to fear death, as Urgathoa ensures that death isn't the end. Through gentle acts of kindness and empathy, they teach people that undeath is Urgathoa's mercy to all mortal kind, a way to save them from their mortal dread with the promise that immortality awaits all who accept it.

The Ashen Church's compassion isn't limited to the living. While most people look upon an undead creature with revulsion or terror, the Ashen Church sees a being that deserves respect and affection. Their very presence can quell the aggression of otherwise malevolently ravenous undead. It's through this peaceful conduct that the Ashen Church has so triumphantly opened the minds and hearts of Golarion's people to Urgathoa and undeath, allowing her name and mercy to spread forever more.

The Savoring Society.name: The Savoring Society
The Savoring Society.text:
The Savoring Society

On the surface, the Savoring Society is an eccentric and exclusive club made up of the wealthiest politicians, merchants, and nobility of Absalom. However, behind gilded doors is a cult that allows the upper class to freely indulge in the pleasures that privilege provides. For these hedonistic aristocrats, gluttony and luxury are their given due, and Urgathoa is their patron who ensures the party never stops.

Members boast of tasting every living thing that has existed across Golarion while sipping wine aged for a thousand years. Opulent gatherings can last for weeks, as the cult's rules proclaim that members must not only indulge in material joy but also savor it, taking all the time one could ever need and more to enjoy such extravagance. The Savoring Society lures in new members from the rich and powerful elite, plying them with their vices and convincing them that Urgathoa is the only goddess they should revere—for who else understands that to enjoy the benefits of impossible wealth, one must consume the poor?

Cults.name: Cults
Cults.text:
Cults

Festering in the darkness of Golarion like a hungry rot, Urgathoan cults gather in secrecy to worship the Pallid Princess. Whether they act in their own self-interest or in misguided selflessness, no matter if they follow her divine aspect of disease, gluttony, or death, all these cults seek to serve Urgathoa's insatiable will.

Practices.name: Practices
Practices.text:
Practices

Urgathoa demands that her worshippers put personal gratification before all else and cast off the constraints imposed by morality, society, and the mortal body. Many of her followers indulge in extreme hedonism, defying taboo to satiate their appetites of the body and the mind. Casting away self-restraint, worshippers feast upon everything Golarion has to offer, whether that's rare delicacies, poisonous rot, or the flesh and lifeblood of sapient creatures. They experiment with the sensual limitations of their bodies, mixing pleasure and pain as they chase increasingly bizarre and grotesque hungers.

Other followers willingly contract and endure illnesses. By allowing disease and infection to ravage their bodies, Urgathoa's faithful can prove their dedication to a life of limitless indulgence while experiencing novel sensations. Urgathoa often gives visions and divine insights to her followers during the fevered dreams of affliction, and her favored messengers exist in a perpetual sickly state.

Urgathoa's worshippers view undeath as the ultimate transcendence of the mortal body's limitation. Many dream of becoming undead, when they can forever fulfill their desires without the pesky limit of mortality. The more magically gifted practice the art of necromancy, learning how to raise the dead and spit in the eye of the natural order to fulfill their own ambitions. Those unable to realize their post-death fantasies venerate the undead, sometimes to the extent of willingly feeding themselves to their more ravenous peers if only to experience the rapture of death in service to Urgathoa.

The more bloodthirsty of Urgathoa's followers satisfy their cravings for violence by torturing and killing in her name. They seek out congregations who worship Urgathoa's enemies and take delight in massacring them, savoring the symphony of screams and the splatter of warm blood upon skin. The victims who were most adamantly against undeath are then reanimated and sent after their surviving loved ones in a final act of perverse and ironic pleasure.

Urra Lynedon.name: Urra Lynedon
Urra Lynedon.text:
Urra Lynedon

Urgathoa gave Urra Lynedon (experimental female vampire count 9) a new purpose in an otherwise boring immortal life: cultivating diseases like one would rare, exotic flowers. Using the bodies of her devoted mortal consorts, Urra nurtures and breeds strains of bacteria, fungi, and viruses from all across Golarion. She offers the results of her experiments to fellow Urgathoan faithful who seek new sensations or the fever-driven visions from their goddess.

Many-Limbs Kimmato.name: Many-Limbs Kimmato
Many-Limbs Kimmato.text:
Many-Limbs Kimmato

Formerly a physician devoted to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.BNycwu3I21dTh4D9]{Sarenrae}, Kimmato (sorrowful nonbinary halfling herexen 5) had their faith shattered when their spouse died in childbirth. Desperate to be united with their spouse, Kimmato spat in the face of everything they once believed and grafted the still-warm remains of their loved one onto their own body with gruesome surgical precision. This act of blasphemous defiance delighted Urgathoa, who blessed them with undeath and a new title. Many-Limbs Kimmato now vengefully carves a bloody path through Sarenrae's temples and worshippers in the name of Urgathoa, their profanely amalgamated body growing with each new victim, hundreds of arms and legs moving in uncanny unison.

Mother's Maw.name: Mother's Maw
Mother's Maw.text:
Mother's Maw

As the divine representative of Urgathoa, Mother's Maw (enigmatic agender herald 15) soars through the air on leathery bat wings to enact its goddess's will. Surrounded by swarms of buzzing flies and adoring undead thralls, the giant winged skull ferries allies into battle, creates new undead, and shoves enemies into its endless gullet. It does everything and anything that the goddess commands, no matter how destructive or bizarre the task is. When it isn't busy fulfilling Urgathoa's wishes, Mother's Maw searches for novel sensual experiences and partakes in passionate conversation about food, wine, perfume, and the other pleasures of life.

Fjarn.name: Fjarn
Fjarn.text:
Fjarn

Fjarn (veteran male ghoul commander 12) has a hulking form, corpse-gray skin, and an unnerving rictus smile that strike fear in the hearts of anyone unlucky enough to cross his path in battle. Once an Ulfen Linnorm King who died by suicide after he was forced to murder and eat his own honor guard, Fjarn rose from the grave with the taste of forbidden flesh on his tongue. He now wages endless war against Urgathoa's enemies, devouring the corpses of his fallen foes to grow his power. Paladins and warriors devoted to other gods whisper about the horrifying sight of a once regal figure stooping low to gnaw on carrion like a common beast.

Barasthangas.name: Barasthangas
Barasthangas.text:
Barasthangas

Barasthangas (studious female fleshwarp mage 11) was obsessed with the machinations of destruction and anti-life, and so she traveled to the Void and was transformed from an elven mage into an undead one. Her powers are now entwined with the Void, and her flesh is stretched so tautly that bones and tissue are visible through her translucent skin. Now back in the Universe, Barasthangas experiments with the creation of new forms of undead infused with entropic energy, viewing Urgathoa as both patron and co-parent to her profane children. She regularly fuels her magic with the life force of foes, allowing her to stupefy them and turn them into new test subjects.

Prominent Figures.name: Prominent Figures
Prominent Figures.text:
Prominent Figures

Urgathoa's most influential worshippers are revered by some, reviled by many, and feared by all. Driven by hunger and delighting in the freedom of undeath, they're handful of the most gruesome, grotesque, and glorious paragons who faithfully serve the Pallid Princess.

Plots of the Pallid Princess.name: Plots of the Pallid Princess
Plots of the Pallid Princess.text:
Plots of the Pallid Princess

Urgathoa was a mortal woman who so loved indulging in the pleasures of the body and mind that she tore herself from the Boneyard and ascended to godhood. As the goddess of disease, gluttony, and undeath, Urgathoa invites her followers to endlessly feast on all the sensations and experiences Golarion has to offer with little regard to morality or mortality. Hedonists, gluttons, necromancers, and undead all follow in her bloody footsteps, chasing after a life where their desires never go unfulfilled.

Content Warning

This article explores the many manifestations of Urgathoan worship. It includes themes of body horror, cannibalism, disordered eating, vomiting, alcohol, eugenics, disease, intentional transmission of disease, medical negligence, death in childbirth, mass murder, suicide, human experimentation, desecration of the dead, undead, and involuntary reanimation.

Saringallow Gazetteer.name: 萨里伽洛地理志 Saringallow Gazetteer

Places of Interest.name: Places of Interest
Places of Interest.text:
Places of Interest

As a burgeoning city, Saringallow has a mix of old, new, and even historical locations of interest to visit.

A. Gallow Farms: The six Gallow Farms have been responsible for maintaining Saringallow's emergency ration supply since the settlement's establishment. Some are family-run and passed down through the generations, while others have been bought and sold. With the recent formation of slums along the north wall and a rise in theft of crops, the farms are campaigning for a change in mayorship. Gerudina Mezeret (meticulous female halfling farmer 4), the most senior of the owners, is their candidate of choice. Though Gerudina has plans for social housing and punitive measures against unregulated construction, her lack of opinion on other issues is criticized.

B. City Watch Barracks: After the demon bile incident, Saringallow expanded its security. The city watch barrack was established within the Noble Folly's gate. Despite the obvious move to deter youths from sneaking out, guards continue to catch children of all ages attempting the traditional dare of going up the Noble Folly's path.

The barracks is fully equipped with its own watch towers, a training yard, stables, a dormitory for two dozen guards, and a mess hall. Captain Jordis Serelli (determined nonbinary aiuvarin human guard captain 5) runs the squads as tightly as the orphanage they grew up in. Under Jordis's command, the city watch handles matters from pickpockets and nightly rounds in the graveyard, to frequent noise complaints against the new resident band. While Jordis is no Chelaxian sympathizer, they dislike insurgents, believing no matter how noble the organization's intent might be, they would do more harm than good.

C. Gallow's Graveyard: With graves as old as the city, Saringallow's graveyard is a place most avoid except when necessary. Nolaria Wintren (adventurous female human cleric of Erastil 5) surprised many when she volunteered to become the new groundskeeper. Rumors say that she might have taken up the post in an act of adulthood rebellion against her adoptive father, Ildris. Others suggest her attachment to the place is sentimental.

Since taking over the graveyard, Nolaria has cultivated a large canopy of mistletoe as a ward on the area against evil. She prunes the patches frequently to prevent overgrowth. The cuttings are then used by both her and many other artisans in Saringallow to create wearable charms in the form of bracelets or wreathes.

D. Traveler's Square: As its name suggests, Traveler's Square is surrounded by inns, eateries, and stores that cater to those who are passing through Saringallow, usually by the Conerica Highway. The gallows here are a popular attraction despite it being forebodingly functional and guarded by menacing-looking (but polite) city guards. When the weather is pleasant, performers like Maire Phelan often line the perimeter of the square in the morning, both to earn their keep and to serve as a convenient alarm clock for travelers who have overslept.

E. City Hall: Realizing that Saringallow would require a larger administration soon with its growing population, Mayor Trinelli bought this mansion by the triangular Crossroad Plaza several years ago. The old town hall was given to the city guard to use as a second office. Much like before, the building contains the mayor's residence, office, and also Saringallow's town records. New additions include a large registry office that keeps track of paperwork, from census to deeds, as well as a cartography department dedicated to surveying rural Saringallow. A courthouse is currently being furnished, though a judge has yet to be officially hired or appointed.

Trinelli's former secretary, Lupia Marietti (curious female human historian 3), has been promoted to City Historian. While her research has uncovered curious records about the Saringallow region before Isger was founded, Lupia has reservations on whether the information should go public during such politically turbulent times.

F. Temple of Erastil: This temple to Old Deadeye is likely the oldest structure in Saringallow, second only to the half-derelict Sarini Manor. While it has undergone many expansions and renovations over the centuries, the building remains dedicated to serving the public. The temple's contribution in health, nutrition, and shelter is the predominant reason why most in Saringallow consider @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.mm1j6UbHqFCI8fwB]{Erastil} to be their patron god. Other faiths, especially those popular in Cheliax, have found it rather difficult to establish a foothold in the city as a result.

Ildris Ruvarra (kind male human cleric of Erastil 6) has served as the head priest to the temple for nearly 20 years. With recent political developments, he's distanced himself from associating with any side, stating he wishes to focus on ensuring the city's food security and agricultural needs. That said, no one—even Hellbreakers who disclose their affiliation—has ever been refused treatment or assistance by the temple's staff or Ildris.

G. Hellbreakers' Headquarters: This two-story residence is difficult to locate unless one has a guide. The Hellbreakers obtained the property at a slight discount after helping the original owners, the Vazarros, restart their life elsewhere. On paper, the property is under Rhokrag's (hardened male hobgoblin warrior 3) name, though Phoebe and Alceo are known “tenants.” The three regularly consecrating the house has endeared them to their neighbors, who respectfully keep quiet whenever Captain Jordis is in the neighborhood.

H. Saringallow's Sundries: The city's co-op venture supplies travelers with general adventuring gear and basic weapons and armor. The store also occasionally sells silver and cold iron weapons, though the demand has long exceeded the supply. Last year, an aviary was added to start a courier pigeon service to major settlements in and out of Isger. Abdil Nestthew (discreet male human scribe 3), hired directly from the partner aviary in Logas, acts as both caretaker to the birds and letter-writer-in-proxy. While the Hellbreakers would love to have Abdil as an ally, Maire's probing so far suggests the young man has an intense dislike for conspiracy and intrigue.

I. Saringallow Orchard: This apple orchard unfortunately suffered from repeated infestations after the demon bile incident. The land was ultimately donated to the Temple of Erastil and consecrated for years to end the vermin problem. After its first successful harvest, a new co-op venture took off.

Today, gallow apple preserves and dried slices have become popular gifts to buy in Saringallow, available at the sundries store and several dockside stalls. The temple intends for the funds to ultimately go toward building a school, though whether that will prevent the youths from skipping their chores, classes, or apprenticeship to hang out in the orchard remains to be seen.

J. Witch's End Tavern: This tavern managed by Alicie Kruptin (tough female human tavern keeper 4) is especially popular with more conservative Saringallow residents, as it implemented a heavy “no magic unless of divinity” policy after the demon bile incident. The entire tavern is under a strong magic suppression field, which has caused a number of issues to even those who might have simply passed by. Exactly who or what Alicie has employed, she refuses to say, other than it's safer than whatever is being prevented on her premise.

K. Dependable Drummady's: Once a simple cobbler shop, Dependable Drummady's is a full-on haberdashery and boutique these days. Drummady Laterna (ambitious female human cobbler 4) expanded her business over the past decade with good word-of-mouth and a sharp eye for fashion that picks up trends faster than Elidir. Though not a full-on member, Drummady has helped the Hellbreakers with disguises many times in the past. Even her staff knows little of her activities since she often conducts them outside of shop hours. As one of the stockholders behind Saringallow's Sundries and the Saringallow Orchard, Drummady holds quite a bit of influence in the city's economic circles.

L. The Lucky Anvil: Ludoff Smeltbristle (boisterous male dwarf blacksmith 5) first visited Saringallow as a tinkerer for his family's caravan from the Five Kings Mountains about a decade ago. He immediately fell in love with Saringallow's surroundings, both nature and urban. After moving to the city proper, he slowly established himself as a reliable smith. A rebel at heart, Ludoff secretly supports the Hellbreakers and crafts items for them in his spare time.

M. Mashnom's Mercs and Mortar: When the Stonechewer goblinoid tribe first moved to Saringallow, they had a difficult time finding those willing to provide housing to the clan. Ultimately, the goblins and hobgoblins decided that, if people won't lease, then they'll just build their own homes. Under the leadership of Mashnom (mute female goblin union leader 5), a vibrant goblinoid community was born in Saringallow. While the unofficial “Chitterstone Road” has many regular businesses that cater to daily needs (with products especially beloved by goblinoids), it's most famous for its construction companies, excellent masons, and mercenary associations.

N. Gerty's Hearty Breads: Claiming “the heartiest damn breads this side o' the river,” this bakery's signage has an additional piece hanging underneath that reads, “Now with Pastries and Pies!” The bakery's owner, Gerty Keronna (stern male human baker 4), spends more time chatting with customers nowadays than at the oven. The chronic pain from his old leg injury from the Goblinblood Wars prevents him from standing for long. Fortunately, his past apprentice Noemi Tauralio (squeamish female human baker 3) has become a baker in her own right. Xerra Bluebottle (kind genderfluid halfling baker 2) is a joy to work with too. The halfling likes to take home leftover bread for the Hellbreakers at the end of the day.

O. Merchant's Square: The Merchant's Square regularly holds auctions for various goods and wares at different hours of the day. Those in the day are a cacophony, while those at night are pleasantly quiet so the nearby residents can rest. Petrello Pindlion (greedy male human fur trader 6), who schedules the auctions, is pretty well known for being willing to move time slots around and “forget” to inform a seller of a schedule change if his commission rates are upped by a percent or two. Petrello has also been making political endeavors, promising to provide tax cuts and establish trade deals with cities outside of Isger through his children. While it's known his son and daughter are in Druma and Cheliax respectively, Petrello's campaign remains speculative for most.

P. Pricknettle's Potions and Poultices: Majara Pricknettle (curt female gnome alchemist 4) is often overworked these days with custom orders for remedies. Rather than take on an apprentice, Majara insists on hiring contract workers instead, especially those who are working hard to establish themselves in the city. As an immigrant from Umok, she knows all too well the struggles of integrating into Saringallow, even if that barrier has lowered considerably in recent times.

Q. Queenly Quriosities: As one of the first shops dedicated to the purchase and sale of magic items, many visitors are decidedly nervous to step beyond the beaded curtains of the front door. To make the experience more entertaining than anxious, the store's proprietor, Lukus Melchian (resolute male gnome harrower 4), adopts the persona of a motherly fortune-teller by the name of “Mama Yaga.” In addition to suggesting the best lucky charms for the season, Mama Yaga always mentions that her extensive private collection of books on all things magical is available to peruse for any whose heart is in the right place.

R. The Fiend's Finale: Once known as the Fortnight Inn, this establishment is a popular spot to dine late into the night. Morvinarr Albusin (superstitious male human innkeeper 3) bought the place a couple of years ago and refurbished the historic inn with his savings. As Alicie's apprentice, Morvinarr's dishes are famously delicious. The innkeeper, however, considers his food a bonus to the real attraction: Saringallow's new resident band, Oasis Rain Showers (outspoken male anadi, male human, female knoll, female elf, and agender aiuvarin human bards 3).

Made up of five Magaambya graduates—one of each branch—Oasis Rain Showers haven't only been influencing Saringallow's cultural scene, their understanding and willingness to explain magic is one of the reasons why Saringallow has softened its attitude toward magic considerably in recent years. That and the famous “sing a Chelaxian loyalist out of town” incident, of course.

S. Beacon Candles Workshop: After the Hellbreakers bought this abandoned warehouse, they discovered it wasn't as inconspicuous as they'd hoped for a headquarters. Gram (mysterious female human chandler 4), one of the oldest Hellbreaker recruits, suggested that they keep it anyway as a decoy. The result is the Beacon Candles Workshop, whose carved candles help fund the Hellbreakers. Gram even worked out a way to pass secret messages by the colors of the candles she makes as well as their carved patterns and shapes.

T. Conerica Docks: Though more boats are docking in Saringallow these days than ever before, Bartle Rudderport (skeptical male human wharfinger 4) keeps meticulous track of all inventory passing through. He's ever concerned of smugglers ruining the reputation of the city. Despite this, Bartle has given the Hellbreakers several second chances and sometimes even points out how the organization could improve their subterfuge.

Relationships and Conflicts.name: Relationships and Conflicts
Relationships and Conflicts.text:
Relationships and Conflicts

Saringallow's reputation is quite pristine these days, and the city maintains good relations with many settlements within Isger, particularly the nearby town of Swiftrun. Within the city, however, there have been more and more interpersonal conflicts. Some are more private in nature that inadvertently spill over into the community, while others are of the public interest. The most likely conflict though is from a source Saringallow has likely not faced before, in recent memory at least: the fey.

Many mourn that the simple settlement has lost its rustic charm, and the fey are no different, chafing at the influx of people and structures. While it isn't the city's fault that no one has communed with the fey in centuries, Saringallow might find itself under attack again if its people don't come to realize the growing grudge of their primal neighbors.

Notable People.name: Notable People
Notable People.text:
Notable People

No one knows where Elleri “Gram” Smalltoes (mysterious female halfling candler 4) came from; some say she's as old as Saringallow itself. The candler mostly keeps to herself except to nag her customers. In truth, Gram was a runaway slave before the Emancipation Edict and harbors a grudge against Cheliax for all its sins against her.

Old Hawk (stubborn male human fearmonger 4) is one of the oldest residents of Saringallow and holds to various superstitions, including lining his house with salt and eating tons of garlic. He's convinced that, one day soon, the Sarinis will descend upon Saringallow to reclaim what was once theirs, and he's determined to be ready for it. Many of the younger folk humor his ravings by accepting garlic garlands and promising to train in fighting, but the older folk are getting tired of his constant fearmongering.

Mayor Sandra Trinelli (prudent female human mayor 6) believes in modernization and reform. This outlook clashes with some of the older residents, who cling to superstition and are wary of change. Slowly but surely, the mayor hopes to pave the way for growth in Saringallow as it teeters on the edge of becoming a potentially major city.

Maire Phelan (jovial female human storyteller 3) has lived in Saringallow for only a short time, settling there after traveling as a storytelling bard. She has witnessed firsthand the neglect and atrocities of the Isgeri government (and implicitly, the Chelaxian government) and knows the people need hope. Using her stories, she works to uplift the people.

Culture and Society.name: Culture and Society
Culture and Society.text:
Culture and Society

Saringallow Holidays

Below are a list of holidays and festivals the city observes in some form or fashion. Unofficial holidays that are developing are marked with an asterisk. Those being phased out are in italics.

  • Abadius: 6th Vault Day; 23rd Steward's Day
  • Calistril: 2th Merrymead; 19th Loyalty Day
  • Pharast: 3th Day of Bones; Vernal Equinox Firstbloom and Planting Week
  • Gozran: 7th Currentseve; 15th Taxfest
  • Desnus: First New Moon Nightgallop; Last Week Shearwalk
  • Sarenith: 6th Vault Day; Summer Solstice Succession
  • Erastus: 3th Archerfeast; Second Week Oaksplit
  • Arodus: 13th Gallows Day; 16th Armasse*
  • Rova: First Week First Brewing; Second Oathday Signing Day; Autumn Equinox Market's Door
  • Lamashan: 21st Snowsow; 30th Allbirth*
  • Neth: 14th Even-Tongue Day; Second Week Harvest Feast
  • Kuthona: Third Week Winter Week; Winter Solstice Loomgather

Closed social circles remain an integral part of Saringallow culture. Folks used to believe that one could live their entire life in the settlement and never meet the soul that will become their neighbor in the graveyard. In some ways, this might be true. As schooling is primarily conducted by one's own family and apprenticeship remains the best path to a career, there isn't a lot of social mobility in Saringallow. One's class and status are often decided upon birth; only adventuring and a decorated military career can predictably break those expectations.

While magic was once greatly feared, that attitude has changed significantly after the Godsrain. Saringallow once saw divine powers as the most reliable—or at least predictably good or evil. Witnessing the death of a god has made many reconsider. Most settled on the sentiment that the intent of the magic user mattered most, not the magic itself. People should be judged by who they are, not what powers they wielded. Anti-magic signage has been taken down, and magic users have been emboldened to be more open about their abilities when they once might have hid them.

One thing that does unite Saringallow is its holidays. While many are observed in Avistan at large, a few are local attractions. There's the Nightgallop, a horse race in rural Saringallow that takes place at night on the first full moon of spring. Succession, on the other hand, is a day when apprentices receive their badge of approval from their teachers in a literal torch-passing ceremony.

Many of the local holidays are then related to agriculture, such as Shearwalk, a week chasing down sheep to shear; Oaksplit, a time when lumber is processed; Snowsow, blessing of the grains that will be used for winter wheat; Harvest Feast, a time of communal meals; and Loomgather, a localized version of the Shelynite Crystalhue. Gallows Day, which commemorates the city's founding, was a somber day of religious observance in the past but has been commercialized recently in an attempt to attract tourism.

Residents.name: Residents
Residents.text:
Residents

Within the walls, Saringallow is home to over 2,500 people. Another 800 or so live beyond the walls in the rural regions, some of which are almost the size of small towns. The population has three major demographics: those who descended from the Sarini servants, those who immigrated here before the Goblinblood Wars, and those who immigrated after. The first group is distinguished by their last or family name as well as their strict adherence to many traditional practices in prayers and superstitions. Some Saringallow laws once gave these families specific privileges in areas such as land or home ownership. Most of these discriminatory laws have been phased out in the recent years.

Saringallow was considered a human settlement before the Goblinblood Wars; nearly all residents without human ancestry today came to reside hereafter. For some, it was because their home was destroyed and beyond salvage. For others, Saringallow's proven safety gave them peace of mind. Halflings and gnomes were among the first to move into the city, while goblins and hobgoblins only started settling in within the last few years. The first of the goblinoids were even paid to move to the city, as Saringallow realized the best way to prevent conflict with the Chitterwood was to accept its people first.

Age is usually a better determiner of how a Saringallow resident acts nowadays. Older residents are more distant, superstitious, stoic, and hardworking. Younger residents and newer immigrants are opportunistic, direct, and open-minded. Those in their teens and under are almost universally mischievous and curious. Regardless of age, nearly all Saringallow folk despise nobility and aristocracy. Even the kindest of noble runaways need to prove themselves before they find acceptance here, which resulted in these scions forming their own private community like everyone else in Saringallow.

Government.name: 政府 Government
Government.text:
Government

Saringallow's mayorship started before the death of the Sarinis and continued on to this day. Originally, the terms were for life. After the first century, Saringallow switched to terms of 5 to 10 years, with the exact number being part of the mayor's proposal during their campaign. This made it easier for Saringallow to see large infrastructural projects through under a single leader. It's tradition for new candidates to start campaigning about two years before the term is up, though there have been occasions when it starts earlier.

While the settlement elects its mayor, Saringallow does answer to Elidir and the Steward of Isger. While most of the city enforces the law by Isgeri standards, there are some times when Saringallow decides to evoke their right to the Old Book. This set of laws is reportedly based on an ancient copy of the Abadaran Manual of City-Building, so ancient that its title actually translates to Laws of Civilization-Building. Some Saringallow locals believe the Old Book to be more friendly for the disenfranchised, especially if they live off the land. Critics of the Old Book point to this reason as to why it shouldn't be used in modern times since its considerations are often unsuitable for an urban environment.

It's undeniable that Saringallow is almost a proper city; it just needs to properly divide itself into districts, name its streets, and number its buildings. While Mayor Trinelli has less than a full year left in her term, she has significantly increased the city hall's administrative capabilities to prepare for this project. This preparation accidentally ended up being a boon when the Steward implemented a new tax for the ongoing war. Many needed it to be deferred, and without the increase in staff to complete all the paperwork, Saringallow might have been squeezed dry.

History.name: History
History.text:
History

The Demon Bile Incident

The incident of demonic corruption and demon bile mentioned in this gazetteer is a reference to the Pathfinder module Gallows of Madness. You can read (or even play) through this module for the full context of this incident, where mysterious events occur at the old abandoned Sarini Estate.

Everyone knows Saringallow as the place founded on the lynching of the Chelaxian noble house of Sarini. The noble house's servants would go mysteriously missing until residents had enough and dealt with the Sarinis themselves. Witch hunts mired the settlement's first decade of self-rule. Those in the rural regions recall it as a time of dogma. Their ancestors risked cultivating the wilderness outside the walls, for to live in Saringallow then was to live in intense paranoia. The settlement struggled financially, as without a manor to serve, there were no goods coming in through the docks.

The Conerica River ultimately saved the settlement from dissolution, for Saringallow managed to stabilize its economy by serving as a rest stop for those traveling north and south. In time, those traveling by road began using it as a stop as well, sometimes as passersby, sometimes to trade with those on the river.

Saringallow's growth was slow for the next two centuries, fueled mostly by those who left to find fortune and returned upon success. Most who tried returned empty-handed if they returned at all. Things changed as the town's third century rolled in, for the Goblinblood Wars were on the horizon. During the wars, Saringallow persevered. Though the locals called their walls the Pauper's Roof, the ramparts were anything but poor in quality. Surviving the war intact gave Saringallow a head start on recovery.

Unbeknownst to most, the site where Saringallow is today was known as the Crosspaths in older, ancient days. Lying almost at the heart of Isger, it was a regular place where those who lived on the lands between the Aspodell and Menador mountains met, usually to reaffirm their alliance. The Sarinis specifically chose to construct their manor here, for it allowed their guests to entertain themselves with some amateur archaeology. At one point, a beautiful glaive was unearthed from the village. The pristine historical artifact was sent to Elidir, where it stayed ever since.

Saringallow.name: 萨里伽洛 Saringallow
Saringallow.text:
Saringallow

Isger's status as a mistreated vassal state of Cheliax overshadows much of the nation's past. For seven centuries, Chelaxian and Isgeri noble houses plundered what resources the land had to offer. What wealth was gained from the lumber, minerals, and gems harvested, generations of ruling stewards squandered. Though threats rose and dangers imperiled, the rich and powerful cared only for the flow of coin on the waters of the Conerica River. And so, whenever the common folk of Isger suffered strife—be it famine, disease, or war—they often faced it alone.

The Goblinblood Wars from nearly three decades ago exemplified this neglect. The Chitterwood hordes razed entire rural communities while the Isgeri army failed to make a timely response. Hedvend VI, then only a couple of years into his stewardship, issued token military orders to protect assets of the upper class and the capital. As more settlements succumbed, waves of soldiers deserted their posts, further lowering morale and straining resources. The violence of the Goblinblood Wars thus inevitably spread beyond the nation.

By the time Isger's neighbors intervened, both banks of the Conerica were overrun. Miraculously, the riverside town of Saringallow stood relatively unscathed amid the wreckage. Protected by its historic ramparts, this defense attracted not only refugees but also soldiers looking to recuperate. That the town's location by the river expedited travel to all corners of Isger was another strategic boon for retreating action or reinforcements.

Convenience, however, didn't automatically translate to support. Saringallow was but a small settlement back then, with plans to shelter 2,000 denizens at most. Without official resupply channels from the government, the town's food stores shrank quickly from the influx of people. Alarmed, the then-mayor passed a highly controversial ordinance upon the foreign forces. Each soldier was allowed a meal and a night of rest per week. Those wounded could stay a fortnight but would consequently be barred from town for a month.

Predictably, many locals disagreed with the absurd rules and began circumnavigating it. They took strangers into their homes, claiming them to be distant cousins or similar relations. Some even risked foraging, fishing, or hunting outside the walls to privately resupply the troops. However suspicious they were of outsiders, the inhabitants of Saringallow knew Isger needed help. If there was a time to defy law and culture for the good of the nation, it was then or never again.

Allegedly, sheltering foreign troops in secrecy was how the unlikely alliance between the Eagle Knights, Hellknights, and Mercenary League started. Claims purport three commanders awkwardly discovered each other's true affiliations while hiding under the same false identity and roof. After coming clean, the three recognized their shared goal. Even when their generals refused to ally over philosophical differences, the commanders tacitly coordinated their troop movements anyway. Several victories later, the reluctant higher-ups acknowledged the effectiveness of cooperation and established a formal alliance… or so the Saringallow folklore whisper.

The famed alliance saved Isger at an immense cost. Death took with it many who witnessed how the coalition formed. Capitalizing on the uncertainty to hide his incompetence, Hedvend VI insinuated he was the one who secretly brought the heroes together. When Saringallow attempted to suggest otherwise, the steward warned he might direct recovery efforts and future protection toward more “important” locations. Yet full of refugees, Saringallow held its tongue to survive and rebuild. For years, it reverted back to the town known only for its grim name, tragic past, and superstitions.

The past Saringallow hides from—be it the city's own founding or the role it played in the Goblinblood Wars—speaks a simple truth: the settlement was always meant to be a stage on which rebellions against establishments, dogma, or tyranny played out. What manifests as paranoia was at its heart a wariness toward power.

Since recovering from a demonic corruption crisis, a renewed growth has revived a spark of that destiny in Saringallow. While the young city yet maintains the tradition of exclusive social circles, the spaces in between have allowed those who would've been enemies in the past to reconcile. People now maintained the traditional social distance not out of fear, but rather to abstain from superficial judgment. For the modern Saringallow, actions in times of crisis measured one's trustworthiness most truly. As the red haze of a nascent war approaches from the horizon, Saringallow once again readies itself to bear witness to what's to come next in Isger's future, whether it be a turn for the better or one for the worse.

Cautious and Wary Residents of Saringallow think twice about what they see, hear, and otherwise perceive. Once per day, creatures who have lived in the city for a week (cumulatively) can reroll a failed Perception check or Will save with a +2 item bonus when they're within Saringallow. Whenever a Saringallow local ties with an adversary's initiative roll, the local goes first.

Superstition Savvy Saringallow has a rich tradition of gestures, phrases, or tokens for many situations. One is bound to work for whatever problem is at hand. Once per month, a creature who has lived in Saringallow for a least a week (cumulatively) can take a free action with the concentrate, linguistic, and manipulate traits when they attempt a skill check to roll twice and take the better result; this is a fortune effect. In addition, Saringallow sells common talismans up to twice its settlement level.

Viro Ahala.name: 维罗·阿哈拉 Viro Ahala
Viro Ahala.text:
Viro Ahala Vengeful Hellknight Armiger

Viro Ahala was born in Egorian to a successful, but not ridiculously wealthy, merchant family. He was afforded quite a few advantages growing up: good schooling, delicious food, and copious free time for athletic or academic hobbies. He lived as the epitome of Chelaxian privilege, studying under very good (but not the best) tutors and lacking nothing.

When Viro was nine, he saw Her Infernal Majestrix Abrogail Thrune II in person for the first time. His family was attending the public execution of several impudent halfling servants who'd dared protest against their masters. Abrogail Thrune also made an appearance, from the safety of a high balcony overlooking the square. Even from a distance, Viro could sense her imperious power; all those in attendance fell silent when she raised her hand to pronounce judgment on the criminals… until the protesters began to shout.

A small group of Egorian citizens were incensed at this execution, yelling that it was “unfair” and “barbaric.” The halflings' crimes were minor—just a little civil disobedience—and they didn't deserve death, according to the protesters. Their demonstration lasted less than five minutes, as a pair of heavily armored Hellknights pushed their way through the crowd and quickly beat the protesters into unconsciousness. With a nod from Abrogail, they were unceremoniously dragged onto the square's dais and summarily executed alongside the halflings.

Right then, Viro Ahala knew what he wanted to do with his life.

He knew he would never rise to the same heights of power as Her Infernal Majestrix—his family's station and lineage saw to that—but being the ironclad fist wielded by such a person appealed to his young mind. He spent the next decade training his mind and his body. He read every book he could get his hands on about the history of the Hellknights and the ordered structure of Hell they sought to emulate. He found a lot to admire in those tomes and scrolls. “This is the way the world should be,” he soon thought. “The smartest and strongest should rule, and the rest should be grateful for such oversight.” When not studying, Viro exercised and practiced his martial prowess. He knew he would have to grow strong enough to wear the massive plate armor that's iconic to the Hellknight orders. His family fully supported this endeavor, as they too were ardent Thrune loyalists.

Eventually, Viro passed the trial to become a Hellknight armiger with the Order of the Rack. It was the proudest day of his life, even if it meant moving to Citadel Rivad near Westcrown. After another year of training, he began to impress his superiors and was stationed with other members of the order in Egorian, ready to crush any dissidence that might arise in the nation's capital. Now, Viro could be just like those Hellknights he witnessed in action over a decade ago.

All was well for months until the Godsrain and Abrogail Thrune's quest to claim any fallen pieces of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.88vRw2ZVPax4hhga]{Gorum}'s body, known as warshards. The Godsrain did little to affect the Hellknights at first. When rumors arose that a faction of rebels in Isger were gathering these very artifacts near the town of Breachill, the Order of Rack was assigned to occupy the area and root out those warshards. Viro was assigned to that company and worked ruthlessly to crush the spirits of Breachill's residents. He had no qualms about using violence against civilians or threatening their livelihoods; they were, after all, simple citizens, while he was someone above them. As he continued to distinguish himself, he knew he would soon become a full Hellknight.

Viro was present at the execution of Reginald Cormoth, though a veteran Hellknight had the honor of wielding the blade. At this point, Viro was certain that the spirit of any resistance was crushed and was surprised as any when Eagle Knights marched on the town, igniting the Battle of Hellknight Hill. Viro fought fervently alongside his comrades and was outside Citadel Altaerein when it was captured. To his chagrin, his regiment was routed by a troop of plucky soldiers allied with the Hellbreakers League, the very group his order was sent to Isger to eliminate. He and a few other Hellknights fled the area but were pursued by League rangers. Viro survived by cowering within an abandoned badger den.

When he emerged, Viro discovered the body of one of his superiors face down in a nearby stream. His mind afire with thoughts of vengeance, Viro stripped the corpse of its armor, taking it for himself. It didn't fit perfectly, too large and unyielding to his form, and it scratched at his neck as if telling him he wasn't yet worthy of it. He told himself he would earn the right to wear it by crushing the Hellbreakers League, but for now, he would use its authority to enact a devious plan.

Campaign Role

Working with the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys, Viro Ahala serves as the main antagonist for Chapters 2 and 3. The sting of losing at the Battle of Hellknight Hill remains with him, and he blames the Hellbreakers League. Their impudence must be punished. And what better way to do so than to summon a devil to help him enact his revenge?

Thanks to a tome he finds with the help of the sisters, Viro has access to a ritual that can summon a powerful devil to empower him to finally put an end to the Hellbreakers. His plans have him moving deep into the Chitterwood, where a source of primal magic in the Stagfall Caves makes the perfect setting for a magic ritual.

The PCs learn of his involvement by the end of @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22202forthe]{Chapter 2} and must track him through the Chitterwood in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22203devils]{Chapter 3}. By the end of their exploration of Stagfall Caves, the PCs have likely slain Viro, who's too much of a zealot to surrender in a fight, especially with his plan so close to fruition.

However, that doesn't have to be the last the PCs see of Viro. Once his soul has been judged, he returns as a diabolic antagonist granted to Caeto Vulaunex in the later chapters of the adventure. At this point, his thirst for vengeance has only intensified, but now the PCs are the main focus of his ire!

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.hellbreakers-bestiary.Actor.t4FFJKVeYLagjBYs]{Viro Ahala}Creature 5

Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias.name: Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias
Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias.text:
Alceo Demetrias and Phoebe Demetrias Leaders of the Hellbreakers League

Alceo grew up in Egorian with his elven mother, who fondly remembered and quietly taught him about life before the Thrune Ascendancy. Those lessons led him to Milani, and he eventually formed an underground network to help people escape from Cheliax. But his efforts were discovered during the Glorious Reclamation, and he fled east. That's where Phoebe met him.

A former Isgeri army officer, Phoebe deserted during the Goblinblood Wars when she realized the military wasn't protecting citizens. She then made a meager living as a mercenary, taking jobs she felt met her moral code. After she saved Alceo from a group of pursuing dottari, he hired her to protect him as he made his way to Andoran. As the two traveled east—dealing with near-constant danger while avoiding the Conerica Straits to throw off pursuit—they realized they worked well together and had much in common. By the time they reached Isger's eastern border, they were in love and decided to remain in the country to help its people together.

Campaign Role

Alceo and Phoebe have led the Hellbreakers League since its founding in 4722 ar. They largely play a background role in this Adventure Path. They see the PCs' potential to be the future leaders of the Hellbreakers League and want to give the PCs the freedom to grow into that role. When they're in direct contact, starting in @UUID[JournalEntry.pf2ap22204intoth]{Chapter 4}, Alceo and Phoebe offer guidance and encouragement to the PCs, each in their own style: Alceo with stirring words, while Phoebe seeks to bolster their martial prowess.
